job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

response.passage: On the evening of October 12th, young Rohan and his grandfather, Dada, sat on the veranda in Jaipur. The sun was setting, casting long, orange shadows across the courtyard. Rohan noticed his own shadow stretched out behind him, reaching nearly 5 meters long. 'Dada, why is my shadow so long now, but it was short at noon?' he asked. Dada smiled and explained, 'Light travels in straight lines. When the sun is low, the light hits you at an angle, creating a longer shadow. At noon, the sun is directly overhead, so the light hits from above, resulting in a much shorter shadow.' Rohan then held up his brass toy elephant. He noticed that the elephant blocked the light, creating a dark patch on the floor. 'The toy is opaque, so it stops the light,' Dada added. Rohan remembered his science project about reflections. He took a small mirror and tilted it. Suddenly, a bright spot of light danced on the wall. 'The mirror reflects the light beam,' Rohan cheered. They watched the light until 6:30 PM, when the sun finally disappeared behind the distant Aravalli hills, leaving the courtyard in darkness.
response.summary: Rohan and his grandfather observe how the position of the sun changes the length of shadows in their courtyard. They also experiment with how opaque objects block light and how mirrors reflect it.
